A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NARRATIVETRACK, with matching authors, benchmark, pipeline and core experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, detection and tracking validation, annotation-quality measurements, and temporal-reasoning and frame-density ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds model evaluations, a post-cleaning human assessment and likelihood-based evaluation results.

M1.justification: Appendix 9.5 adds an optional answer-selection procedure that scores candidates by normalized conditional likelihood and selects the highest-scoring answer. The entity-extraction pipeline, CRP dimensions and underlying model architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use AVA, Video-MME and LVBench sources for the same 1,006-question benchmark and retain the same reasoning dimensions and scenarios. V2's explicit human-only scope and newly reported 406-clip count clarify existing coverage; they do not establish a changed population or task.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LLaVA-Video-7B while retaining the distinct LLaVA-NeXT-Video models. Section 3.1 adds an OWLv2-only detection comparator alongside Detectron2 and the ensemble. GPT-4o's additional frame configuration changes settings rather than comparator identity.

E3.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o evaluation at 20 frames, matching the open-source models' frame budget while retaining its 128-frame evaluation. Appendix 9.5 introduces likelihood-based evaluation, and Section 3.3 reports an additional three-annotator assessment after cleaning. The original benchmark protocols remain represented.

E4.justification: New analyses examine answer-selection sensitivity through likelihood-based evaluation, GPT-4o performance under a matched frame budget, and cleaned-benchmark reliability through human assessment. The OWLv2-only result extends the detector-ensemble ablation. Existing temporal-direction, distractor, frame-density and reversed-video analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The 100-item, three-annotator audit, Fleiss' kappa of 0.767 and existing plotted uncertainty displays are retained. The new human and likelihood-based accuracies are point estimates; no new seed information, repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: All retained numerical rows in Tables 2 and 9 match. New Table 2 averages are 34.39% for LLaVA-Video-7B and 70.97% for GPT-4o at 20 frames; its 128-frame result remains 72.27%. V2 also adds OWLv2 recall of 0.801, post-cleaning mean human accuracy of 96%, and Table 10 likelihood-based averages of 46.82% and 37.97%. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix 9.5 newly defines the normalized candidate-likelihood scoring function and its maximum-score selection rule. This is a limited formal addition accompanying the new evaluator. Existing entity-representation, detection-fusion and matching mathematics is unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the core contributions: an entity-centric narrative benchmark, CRP and an automated annotation pipeline. Claims about temporal-perceptual trade-offs, directional bias and limitations of scaling also remain. The revised title and additional evidence do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits applicability to human entities, explains why non-human tracking could confound evaluation, and identifies broader entity coverage as future work. Appendix 9.5 adds interpretations favoring generation-based evaluation and notes that likelihood evaluation is limited to open-source models.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page pointer, the 406-clip count, exact counts by reasoning dimension, more explicit QA-validity and correction criteria, and attribution of the failure examples to Video-LLaMA2-7B. OSNet and detector thresholds were already documented in v1's appendix. The PDFs do not establish that the expanded construction description reflects a newly rebuilt benchmark.

R1.justification: V2 adds VELOCITI and a focused comparison contrasting its localized agent-action entailment with cross-scene entity continuity. The added likelihood evaluator explicitly draws on StrictVLE from that work. The remaining cited works are retained despite bibliography reformatting and renumbering.

P1.justification: V2 substantially revises the abstract, introduction and benchmark-construction exposition. Section 3.3 develops separate discussions of QA formats, distractors and quality review, while appendix templates receive systematic language corrections. The paper is retitled and replaces video-specific terminology with video-specialized terminology throughout much of the prose.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column format, extensively resizing and relocating displays and restyling appendix prompt boxes. V2 redraws Figure 3's distribution chart, adds the QA-construction illustration in Figure 4 and likelihood results in Table 10, and expands Table 2. Most existing experimental plots are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation credibility by adding a 20-frame GPT-4o control to v1's comparison against 20-frame open-source models. Clearer construction and scope explanations, an additional detector comparator and post-cleaning human validation also help. The new human assessment lacks a stated sample size, and Table 10 uses model labels inconsistent with Table 2, limiting those additions. Overall, the gains are useful but incremental.
